syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Chemical reactions and chemical equations

concepts.learning_objective: Identify a chemical reaction from observations such as a change in state, change in colour, evolution of a gas or change in temperature.
Write a word-equation and identify the reactants and products and the direction of a reaction.
Explain why an equation with unequal numbers of atoms on the two sides is a skeletal chemical equation.

topics.title: Balancing chemical equations

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the law of conservation of mass to the need for balancing chemical equations without changing formulae.
Balance chemical equations by the hit-and-trial method using the smallest whole-number coefficients.
Interpret the state symbols (s), (l), (g), (aq) and the reaction conditions written on the arrow.

topics.title: Combination reactions and exothermic reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Identify combination reactions in which two or more substances form a single product.
Explain exothermic reactions using examples such as burning of natural gas, respiration and composting.
Explain the reactions of quick lime with water and of slaked lime with carbon dioxide in whitewashing.

topics.title: Decomposition reactions and endothermic reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Describe thermal decomposition of ferrous sulphate, calcium carbonate and lead nitrate and their products.
Explain decomposition of water by electricity and of silver chloride and silver bromide by sunlight.
Recognise that decomposition reactions absorb energy and are endothermic, unlike combination reactions.

topics.title: Displacement and double displacement reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain displacement of copper from its compounds by more reactive metals such as iron, zinc and lead.
Identify double displacement reactions as an exchange of ions and recognise precipitation reactions.

topics.title: Oxidation and reduction

concepts.learning_objective: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of gain or loss of oxygen or hydrogen.
Identify the substance oxidised and the substance reduced in a redox reaction.

topics.title: Effects of oxidation in everyday life: corrosion and rancidity

concepts.learning_objective: Describe corrosion of metals such as the rusting of iron and the coatings on copper and silver, and ways to prevent it.
Explain rancidity as the oxidation of fats and oils and the methods used to slow it down.

topics.title: Acid-base indicators

concepts.learning_objective: Identify natural and synthetic acid-base indicators and use their colour changes to tell acids from bases.
Explain how olfactory indicators such as vanilla, onion and clove oil show acids and bases by a change in odour.

topics.title: Chemical reactions of acids and bases

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the reactions of acids and of bases with metals, and the test for the hydrogen gas evolved.
Predict the products when metal carbonates and hydrogencarbonates react with acids and test for carbon dioxide.
Explain neutralisation and classify metallic oxides as basic and non-metallic oxides as acidic.

topics.title: What all acids and all bases have in common

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that acids produce H+(aq) ions only in water, which makes their solutions conduct electricity.
Recognise that H+ ions exist as hydronium ions and that bases give OH- ions, soluble bases being alkalis.
Explain why dissolving acids or bases in water is exothermic and why acid must be added to water.

topics.title: Strength of acid and base solutions: the pH scale

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the pH value of a solution to its hydrogen ion concentration and its acidic, neutral or basic nature.
Distinguish strong and weak acids by the amount of H+ ions they produce at the same concentration.

topics.title: Importance of pH in everyday life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of pH in the body, digestion, acid rain and soil for plant growth.
Apply neutralisation to explain tooth decay prevention and remedies for bee and nettle stings.

topics.title: Salts: families, pH and chemicals from common salt

concepts.learning_objective: Group salts into families by their common positive or negative radicals.
Predict whether a salt solution is acidic, basic or neutral from the strength of its parent acid and base.
Describe the chlor-alkali process and the preparation and uses of bleaching powder.

topics.title: Baking soda, washing soda and water of crystallisation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the preparation, reactions and uses of baking soda and washing soda.
Define water of crystallisation and explain the colour change of copper sulphate crystals on heating.
Explain the formation, setting and storage of Plaster of Paris from gypsum.

topics.title: Physical properties of metals and non-metals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe lustre, hardness, malleability, ductility, conduction of heat and electricity and sonority of metals and relate them to uses.
Identify the physical properties of non-metals and the exceptions that make physical properties alone insufficient for classification.

topics.title: Reactions of metals with oxygen, water and acids

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how metals form oxides with oxygen, including basic and amphoteric oxides and protective oxide layers.
Compare the reactions of metals with cold water, hot water and steam and write the products formed.
Explain the reactions of metals with dilute acids, including the special behaviour of nitric acid.

topics.title: Displacement reactions and the reactivity series

concepts.learning_objective: Predict whether a metal will displace another metal from its salt solution.
Use the reactivity series and displacement results to arrange metals in order of reactivity.

topics.title: Ionic compounds and their properties

concepts.learning_objective: Show the formation of ionic compounds by transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal.
Explain the physical nature, melting points, solubility and electrical conduction of ionic compounds.

topics.title: Occurrence and extraction of metals

concepts.learning_objective: Define minerals, ores and gangue and relate the occurrence of metals to their reactivity.
Distinguish roasting from calcination and outline how metals of medium reactivity are extracted.
Choose a suitable reduction method (heat, carbon, displacement or electrolysis) from a metal's place in the activity series.

topics.title: Refining of metals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe electrolytic refining, including the electrodes, the electrolyte and the fate of impurities.

topics.title: Corrosion and its prevention

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the conditions needed for iron to rust from an experiment.
Explain methods of preventing rusting, such as painting and galvanisation.
Explain what alloys are and how alloying changes the properties of metals.

topics.title: Bonding in carbon: the covalent bond

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why carbon forms covalent bonds by sharing electrons rather than forming C4+ or C4- ions.
Identify single, double and triple covalent bonds from electron dot structures of simple molecules.
Relate the low melting points, boiling points and poor conductivity of covalent compounds to their bonding.

topics.title: Versatile nature of carbon: catenation, tetravalency and saturation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how catenation and tetravalency allow carbon to form a very large number of stable compounds.
Distinguish saturated from unsaturated carbon compounds using their bonds and structures.

topics.title: Chains, branches and rings

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise structural isomers as compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures.
Classify hydrocarbons as alkanes, alkenes or alkynes and as open-chain or cyclic compounds.

topics.title: Functional groups, homologous series and nomenclature

concepts.learning_objective: Identify heteroatoms and functional groups and explain how they decide the properties of a compound.
Describe a homologous series and the gradation of physical properties along it.
Name simple carbon compounds using the correct prefix or suffix for the functional group.

topics.title: Chemical properties of carbon compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain complete and incomplete combustion and the nature of the flames they produce.
Explain the oxidation of alcohols to carboxylic acids by oxidising agents.
Distinguish addition reactions of unsaturated hydrocarbons from substitution reactions of saturated ones.

topics.title: Ethanol and ethanoic acid

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the properties and reactions of ethanol with sodium and with hot concentrated sulphuric acid.
Describe the properties of ethanoic acid and its reactions with bases, carbonates and hydrogencarbonates.
Explain the formation of esters and their conversion back by saponification.

topics.title: Soaps and detergents

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how soap molecules form micelles that remove oily dirt.
Explain why soap forms scum in hard water and why detergents remain effective in it.

topics.title: What are life processes?

concepts.learning_objective: Define life processes as the maintenance functions of an organism and name nutrition, respiration, transportation and excretion.
Explain why invisible molecular movement is needed to repair and maintain living structures.
Explain why diffusion is insufficient for multicellular organisms and why specialised tissues and transport are needed.

topics.title: Autotrophic nutrition and photosynthesis

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the raw materials, events and products of photosynthesis and how plants store unused carbohydrate.
Interpret the starch-test activities showing that chlorophyll and carbon dioxide are essential for photosynthesis.
Explain how guard cells open and close stomata and how plants obtain water and minerals such as nitrogen.

topics.title: Heterotrophic nutrition and nutrition in single-celled organisms

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between organisms that break down food outside the body, those that take in whole food, and parasites.
Describe how Amoeba and Paramoecium take in and digest food.

topics.title: Nutrition in human beings

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the roles of teeth, saliva, gastric glands, acid, pepsin and mucus in digestion.
Explain how bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal juice complete the digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats.
Explain how villi absorb digested food and how the large intestine absorbs water.

topics.title: Respiration

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the pathways by which glucose is broken down in yeast, in muscle cells and in mitochondria.
Describe ATP as the energy currency of the cell and how it is made and used.
Explain gaseous exchange in plants, aquatic animals and the human respiratory system.

topics.title: Transportation in human beings

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the flow of blood through the four chambers of the heart and explain double circulation.
Distinguish arteries, veins and capillaries and interpret systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
Describe the roles of platelets in clotting and of lymph in transport.

topics.title: Transportation in plants

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why plants need a transport system and why it can be relatively slow.
Explain how root pressure and transpiration pull move water and minerals up the xylem.
Describe translocation of food in phloem and how it uses energy from ATP.

topics.title: Excretion in human beings and plants

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the organs of the human excretory system and the path of urine.
Explain filtration and selective reabsorption in nephrons and compare the kidney with dialysis.
Describe the ways in which plants get rid of their waste products.

topics.title: Nervous tissue: receptors, neurons and the synapse

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the role of receptors and the parts of a neuron through which information is acquired and conducted.
Explain how a nerve impulse is passed across a synapse to another neuron or to a muscle cell.

topics.title: Reflex actions and the reflex arc

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise reflex actions as quick, automatic responses and explain why they are needed.
Describe the pathway of a reflex arc and the role of the spinal cord in it.

topics.title: The human brain and the central nervous system

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the central nervous system from the peripheral nervous system and describe how they communicate.
Relate the fore-brain, mid-brain and hind-brain (medulla, cerebellum) to the actions they control.

topics.title: Protection of nervous tissue and how muscles act

concepts.learning_objective: State how the brain and spinal cord are protected in the body.
Explain how nerve impulses cause muscle cells to change shape and produce movement.

topics.title: Movements in plants: immediate responses and tropisms

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the sensitive plant responds to touch without nervous or muscle tissue.
Identify phototropism, geotropism, hydrotropism and chemotropism as growth movements towards or away from a stimulus.

topics.title: Chemical communication and plant hormones

concepts.learning_objective: Compare electrical impulses with chemical (hormonal) communication between cells.
State the roles of auxin, gibberellins, cytokinins and abscisic acid in plant growth and responses.

topics.title: Hormones in animals and their regulation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how adrenaline prepares the body to deal with an emergency.
Match endocrine glands with the hormones they secrete and the effects of their deficiency.
Explain how feedback mechanisms and the hypothalamus regulate the timing and amount of hormone release.

topics.title: DNA copying and the importance of variation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the creation of a DNA copy along with additional cellular apparatus is a basic event in reproduction.
Explain why DNA copies are similar but not always identical to the original.
Evaluate how variation helps a species survive when its niche changes.

topics.title: Fission, fragmentation and regeneration

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish binary fission in Amoeba and Leishmania from multiple fission in Plasmodium.
Explain fragmentation in Spirogyra and why complex organisms cannot reproduce cell by cell.
Describe regeneration in Hydra and Planaria and why it differs from reproduction.

topics.title: Budding, vegetative propagation and spore formation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe budding in Hydra and yeast.
Explain vegetative propagation and tissue culture and their advantages.
Describe spore formation in Rhizopus and how spores survive.

topics.title: Why the sexual mode of reproduction?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how combining DNA from two individuals generates more variation.
Explain why germ-cells carry half the DNA and how male and female gametes differ.

topics.title: Sexual reproduction in flowering plants

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the reproductive parts of a flower and distinguish unisexual from bisexual flowers.
Distinguish self- and cross-pollination and describe how fertilisation occurs.
Describe how the ovule and ovary develop after fertilisation and how a seed germinates.

topics.title: Puberty and the male reproductive system

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the changes at puberty and explain why they occur when body growth slows.
State the functions of the testes, vas deferens, urethra and accessory glands.

topics.title: Female reproductive system and menstruation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the organs of the female reproductive system and the site of fertilisation.
Explain how the placenta nourishes the embryo and removes its wastes.
Explain why menstruation occurs when the egg is not fertilised.

topics.title: Reproductive health

concepts.learning_objective: Identify bacterial and viral sexually transmitted diseases and how their spread can be reduced.
Distinguish barrier, hormonal, intrauterine and surgical methods of contraception.
Evaluate the importance of a healthy sex ratio and the issue of female foeticide.

topics.title: Accumulation of variation during reproduction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how variations accumulate over generations and why sexual reproduction creates more diversity than asexual reproduction.
Explain how environmental selection of variants helps some individuals survive better.

topics.title: Inherited traits and Mendel's monohybrid cross

concepts.learning_objective: Identify inherited traits and their variants, such as free and attached earlobes, in human populations.
Describe Mendel's cross between tall and short pea plants and predict F1 and F2 results.
Distinguish dominant and recessive traits and use them to interpret inheritance data.

topics.title: Inheritance of two traits: independent inheritance

concepts.learning_objective: Work out the F1 and F2 progeny of a cross involving two pairs of contrasting traits.
Explain how new combinations of traits in the F2 generation show that traits are inherited independently.

topics.title: How traits are expressed: genes, proteins and chromosomes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a gene controls a trait by providing information for a protein such as an enzyme.
Explain how chromosomes and germ cells with a single gene set ensure equal contribution of both parents.

topics.title: Sex determination

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the different ways in which sex is determined in different species.
Explain how the X and Y chromosomes determine the sex of a child in human beings.

topics.title: Reflection of Light and Plane Mirrors

concepts.learning_objective: State and apply the two laws of reflection, measuring angles from the normal.
Describe the image formed by a plane mirror (virtual, erect, same size, laterally inverted, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front) and use it in everyday situations.

topics.title: Spherical Mirrors: Terms, Image Formation and Ray Diagrams

concepts.learning_objective: Define the pole, centre of curvature, principal axis, principal focus, focal length and aperture of a spherical mirror, and use R = 2f.
Describe the image a convex mirror forms of a real object.
Use the standard rays (parallel to the axis, through F, through C, at the pole) to draw ray diagrams for spherical mirrors.
Predict the position, size and nature of the image a concave mirror forms for each position of the object.

topics.title: Uses of Spherical Mirrors, Sign Convention, Mirror Formula and Magnification

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the uses of concave and convex mirrors from the images they form.
Apply the New Cartesian sign convention to distances and heights for spherical mirrors.
Calculate and interpret the magnification m = h'/h = -v/u of a spherical mirror.
Use the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f to find an unknown distance.

topics.title: Refraction of Light and the Rectangular Glass Slab

concepts.learning_objective: Explain refraction as a change of direction caused by a change of speed at a boundary, and say when light bends towards or away from the normal.
Trace a ray through a rectangular glass slab and explain the emergent ray and its lateral displacement.
Explain everyday effects of refraction such as a raised coin, a shallow-looking pool and a bent pencil.
State and apply the laws of refraction, including Snell's law.

topics.title: Refractive Index

concepts.learning_objective: Define absolute and relative refractive index and interpret their values.
Compare media by optical density and distinguish it from mass density.
Calculate the refractive index of one medium with respect to another and predict the direction of bending.
Relate refractive index to the speed of light in a medium (n = c/v) and calculate speeds and times.

topics.title: Spherical Lenses: Image Formation and Ray Diagrams

concepts.learning_objective: Identify convex and concave lenses and define the optical centre, principal foci and focal length.
Predict the position, size and nature of the image a convex lens forms for each position of the object, and relate them to its uses.
Use the standard rays (parallel to the axis, through a focus, through the optical centre) to draw ray diagrams for lenses.
Describe the image a concave lens forms of a real object.

topics.title: Lens Formula, Magnification and Power of a Lens

concepts.learning_objective: Define the power of a lens, its unit (dioptre) and sign, and convert between power and focal length.
Find the power of thin lenses in contact by adding their powers.
Use the lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f with the New Cartesian sign convention.
Calculate and interpret the magnification m = h'/h = v/u of a lens.

chapters.title: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

topics.title: The human eye: structure and image formation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the parts of the human eye (cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina) and state the function of each.
Describe how a real, inverted image formed on the retina is converted into signals that the brain interprets.

topics.title: Power of accommodation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the ciliary muscles change the curvature and focal length of the eye lens to focus near and distant objects.
State the near point and far point of a normal eye and the range of distinct vision.
State what cataract is and how vision can be restored.

topics.title: Defects of vision and their correction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the causes of myopia and calculate the power of the concave lens that corrects it.
Explain the causes of hypermetropia and calculate the power of the convex lens that corrects it.
Explain presbyopia and the use of bi-focal lenses for people with both near and distant vision defects.

topics.title: Refraction of light through a prism

concepts.learning_objective: Trace the incident, refracted and emergent rays through a triangular glass prism and the bending at each face.
Define the angle of the prism and the angle of deviation, and contrast a prism with a glass slab.

topics.title: Dispersion of white light and the rainbow

concepts.learning_objective: Define dispersion and explain why different colours of white light bend through different angles in a prism.
Interpret Newton's experiment with two prisms as evidence that white light is made of seven colours.
Explain how raindrops refract, disperse and internally reflect sunlight to form a rainbow opposite the Sun.

topics.title: Atmospheric refraction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why stars twinkle and planets do not, using atmospheric refraction.
Explain advance sunrise, delayed sunset and the wavering of objects seen through hot air.

topics.title: Scattering of light

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Tyndall effect as scattering of light by colloidal particles and relate scattered colour to particle size.
Explain the blue colour of the sky, the dark sky at high altitudes and the use of red danger signals.

topics.title: Electric current and circuit

concepts.learning_objective: Define electric current as the rate of flow of charge, use I = Q/t and state the ampere and the conventional direction of current.
Explain that current flows only in a closed circuit and that an ammeter is connected in series to measure it.

topics.title: Electric potential, potential difference and circuit diagrams

concepts.learning_objective: Define potential difference as work done per unit charge, use V = W/Q and state the volt.
Identify the voltmeter connection and the standard symbols used in circuit diagrams.

topics.title: Ohm's law

concepts.learning_objective: State Ohm's law and interpret the straight-line V-I graph of a metallic conductor at constant temperature.
Use R = V/I and I = V/R to relate current to resistance and describe the role of a rheostat.

topics.title: Factors on which resistance depends; resistivity

concepts.learning_objective: Apply R = rho l / A to predict how resistance changes with length and area of cross-section.
Use resistivity to compare conductors, alloys and insulators and justify their uses.

topics.title: Resistance of a system of resistors

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate equivalent resistance, current and potential differences for resistors in series.
Calculate equivalent resistance and branch currents for resistors in parallel.
Choose and analyse combinations of resistors to obtain a required resistance.

topics.title: Heating effect of electric current and its applications

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Joule's law H = I^2 R t to calculate and compare the heat produced in resistors.
Explain the working of electric bulbs, heating appliances and fuses using the heating effect.

topics.title: Electric power and commercial unit of energy

concepts.learning_objective: Use P = VI = I^2 R = V^2/R and the watt to calculate the power of electrical devices.
Calculate electrical energy in kW h and joules and estimate the cost of electricity used.

topics.title: Magnetic field and field lines

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a magnetic field and how its direction at a point is fixed using a compass needle.
State and apply the properties of magnetic field lines of a bar magnet.

topics.title: Magnetic field due to a current through a straight conductor

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that a current-carrying straight wire produces a magnetic field of concentric circles around it.
Explain how the field of a straight wire depends on the current and on the distance from the wire.

topics.title: Right-hand thumb rule

concepts.learning_objective: Use the right-hand thumb rule to find the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor.

topics.title: Magnetic field of a circular loop and a solenoid

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the magnetic field of a current-carrying circular loop and coil.
Describe the magnetic field inside and around a current-carrying solenoid.
Explain how a solenoid is used to make an electromagnet.

topics.title: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the factors that decide the direction and size of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
Apply Fleming's left-hand rule to find the direction of force on a conductor or moving charge.

topics.title: Domestic electric circuits

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the wires, supply values and parallel connection used in domestic circuits.
Explain the role of the earth wire as a safety measure.
Explain short-circuiting and overloading and how a fuse protects a circuit.

topics.title: Ecosystem and its components

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the biotic and abiotic components of an ecosystem and distinguish natural from human-made ecosystems.
Explain the roles of producers, consumers and decomposers and how they depend on one another.

topics.title: Food chains, trophic levels and food webs

concepts.learning_objective: Place organisms of a food chain at the correct trophic level and consumer category.
Explain why feeding relationships form branching food webs rather than single straight chains.

topics.title: Flow of energy in an ecosystem

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the 10 percent rule to calculate energy available at successive trophic levels.
Explain why energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional and diminishes at each level.

topics.title: Biological magnification

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how non-degradable chemicals accumulate progressively along a food chain.
Describe how pesticides from fields enter food chains through soil and water.

topics.title: Ozone layer and its depletion

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how ozone forms in the upper atmosphere and how it shields the Earth from UV radiation.
Relate the drop in ozone to CFCs and evaluate steps taken to limit the damage.

topics.title: Managing the garbage we produce

concepts.learning_objective: Classify substances as biodegradable or non-biodegradable and explain the role of enzyme specificity.
Evaluate everyday practices and choices for reducing and disposing of waste.
